correctness.rationale: With P=q+(r-q)(1-e^-s), F=Dkl(P||q), G=Dkl(q||P), H=B(1-e^-s)+chi s: exact derivatives yield log(F_prime/H_prime) derivative T(s)-chi e^s/(B+chi e^s), where T decreases from infinity to 0 and the second term strictly increases. Hence unique crossing and strict global maxima, separately for F/s. The exact identity (P-q)(logit P-logit q)=F+G produces the reverse-KL stationary inverse. Taylor expansions at P=r and s=s_P prove the small-cost logarithmic time/chi log chi efficiency and large-cost 1/chi expansions. Independently verified reverse-KL derivative and three bisection optimizers, not proof by sampling.

final_claim: For fixed interior Bernoulli populations 0<q<r<1 and housekeeping chi>0, finite-affinity charging efficiency has exactly one optimum s_chi>s_P, strictly decreasing with chi and exactly inverted by chi=B e^(-s)Dkl(q||P(s))/(Dkl(P(s)||q)-sF_prime(s)), with sharp small/large housekeeping asymptotics.
limitations: Fixed q,r in (0,1), q<r and chi>0, exponential relaxation and constant housekeeping; no uniformity at population boundaries.
